articleTitle: Implementation a hybrid MAS and SPA algorithm for broadband electromagnetic induction problems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 7th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: The computational complexity/efficiency of the method of auxiliary sources (MAS) is significantly reduced at high frequency (high induction number >40) for electromagnetic induction problems. At the same time the small penetration-depth approximation (SPA) is very accurate at high frequency/induction numbers. A hybrid algorithm, combining the MAS with SPA, is efficiently implemented. Numerical experiments are performed for a highly conducting and permeable sphere and a prolate spheroid under a time varying primary magnetic field. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed method is able to produce very accurate results with low computational requirements.

articleTitle: Efficient FDTD simulation of fields in coaxial cables with multi-layered insulation partially formed by dispersive layers of extremely high permittivity
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 7th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: An efficient and accurate FDTD simulation technique for investigation of field propagation in multi-layered coaxial cables has been developed. This technique combines a uniform FDTD scheme with the piecewise linear recursive convolution method, which is applied for the treatment of fields in dispersive layers, having extremely high permittivity. The method has been developed and tested for a radial symmetric cylindrical system and is intended for future use in 3D applications.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic imaging for a conducting cylinder buried in the three layers structure
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 7th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: The paper presents a computational approach to the imaging of a conducting cylinder buried in the three layers structure. A conducting cylinder of unknown shape, which is buried in the second layer scatters the incident wave from the first layer and the scattered field is recorded in the first and third layers. Based on the boundary condition and the measured scattered field, a set of nonlinear integral equations is derived and the imaging problem is optimized by the genetic algorithm. Numerical results demonstrated that, even when the initial guess is far away from the exact one, good reconstruction has been obtained.

articleTitle: Modified phase problem with nonsymmetrical data
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 7th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: The so-called modified phase problem is associated, in particular, with, linear antenna synthesis by the given amplitude radiation pattern. Using explicit solutions of the problem, the case of a nonsymmetrical given function is analyzed. Numerical results are compared with those for the symmetrical case.

articleTitle: Bicriterion optimization problems for power transmitting line
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 7th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: Two bicriterion optimization problems consisting of the minimization of functionals, describing the energy and ecology requirements (transmission efficiency, surface usage, side radiation) are considered. A numerical method is proposed and results are presented.

articleTitle: Analytical-numerical investigation of the nonlinear equation for a synthesis problem of waveguide array
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 7th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: The nonlinear equation of a synthesis problem for the waveguide array using a standard technique of the calculus of variations is obtained. Utilization of the Bubnov-Galerkin method for the solution of a direct problem (analysis problem) allows for certain restrictions to obtain a real kernel of this equation. The existence of a real kernel enables to carry out analytical investigation of the non-uniqueness and branching of solutions of the obtained equation. Numerical results of research of the eigen values of the corresponding-linear equation are given.

articleTitle: Experimental and numerical investigation of pear-shaped antenna
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 7th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: A further investigation for the pear shaped metallic antenna covered with a thin dielectric layer is presented. Antenna radiation characteristics' dependence on its geometry and electromagnetic parameters has been studied. The prototype of such an antenna has been prepared and measurements have been conducted. The comparison between the numerical and experimental results is given.

articleTitle: The asymmetry of the near field of nonsuperdirected small antenna
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 7th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: The evaluation of the possibility of the near field asymmetry for the small resonant antenna with a smooth distribution of electric field on its surface is given. The antennas with the asymmetry field in the near domain can be used in many technical applications (electromagnetic compatibility, mobile phone and so on). The asymmetry is not present in the radiation pattern (except for the case when antenna has a very prolate shape).

articleTitle: About evaluation of the potential integrals for near field calculations in MoM solution to EFIE for triangulated surfaces
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 7th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: An analytical evaluation is given of potential integrals for near field calculations of electromagnetically excited triangulated structures. An application of the derived expressions for calculating the near field of a simple car model is shown in comparison with the results obtained by well-known code.

articleTitle: Diffraction by a thin-walled plane inclusion of arbitrary rigidity: the case of SH-waves
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 7th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: A thin plane inclusion is perfectly bonded to a surrounding elastic matrix (in two-dimensional Euclidean space) and subjected to an incident plane harmonic SH wave. Using the representation theorem for the displacements the problem is described by singular integral equations. The solutions. to the integral equations for the wave zone of the inclusion are presented in a closed form that is computationally effective and yields accurate results in the resonance region of dimensionless wave numbers. The method of investigation is based on the Wiener-Hopf technique.

articleTitle: Wave scattering by semi-infinite discrete structures
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 7th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: A new approach to the construction of the theory of electromagnetic wave scattering by periodic sequences of partly transparent screens is suggested. A periodic sequence is either an infinite structure of equidistant plane screens, or a semi-infinite or finite part of such a structure. The operator of the reflection by a semi-infinite periodic structure is most essential in the developed theory. A periodic strip array is considered mainly as an element of the multi-layered structure.

articleTitle: Flat microwave antennas for telecommunication systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 7th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: In this paper it is shown, that reflectarrays have inherent advantages over parabolic reflector antennas and, hence, there is interest in using these antennas as replacements for standard reflectors. Numerical investigations of reflective type antennas with flat reflectors are discussed. Also, we have measured the scattering parameters of controllable microstrip reflectarrays. The research can be used to develop antennas with optimum parameters.

articleTitle: Investigation of the resonance characteristics of the carcase
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 7th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: We present a numerical study of EMC/EMI problems related to the resonance enhancement of the electromagnetic (EM) field inside vehicles, its influence on the passengers and on the internal sensitive electronic devices. To this problem we have applied the method of auxiliary sources (MAS) which proves to be convenient in the cases presented here. The resonance curves were obtained for various simplified models of a car body.

articleTitle: Numerical comparison of two methods for irregular waveguide
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 7th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: Two methods of solving the problem of scattering in irregular waveguides are compared. The methods are used to calculate the field in waveguides with smooth and non-smooth irregularities. Numerical results showing the efficiency of those methods are presented.

articleTitle: Ray acousto-elasticity integrals for 2-D strain field
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 7th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: Starting from the equations of dynamics of a small disturbance in a strained continuum, integral acousto-elasticity relations, that connect the mean phase velocities of plane waves of different polarizations to the strain distribution in the direction of the wave propagation, have been established.

articleTitle: A theory of symmetric dipole formed of thin rectangular metallic plates
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 7th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: Basing on the theory of generalized /spl delta/-like functions, a theory of the symmetric dipole formed of thin rectangular metallic plates has been developed. An integral equation for the surface current density was derived and its rigorous solution at h///spl lambda//spl Gt/1 (h - the dipole length, /spl lambda/ - the wavelength) was constructed. The analytical expression for the dipole directivity characteristic and input resistance was also defined.

articleTitle: The exact solution of the problem of ultrawideband signals radiation by a TEM-horn
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 7th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: The exact solution of the problem of ultrawideband signal radiation by a TEM-horn based on the solution of the Fredholm integral equation of the second kind for "jumping" of current using the Meixner boundary conditions is proposed.

articleTitle: Scattering by dihedral conductive wedge cylindrically tipped and concentric multilayered dielectric coated
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 7th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: In the presented study the rigorous solution of the problem in closed-form is obtained. The boundary-value method using the property of completeness of angular functions on a certain interval is employed to obtain the solution. The back radar cross section (BRCS) of the structure is evaluated asymptotically and numerical results with controlled accuracy are presented in case of H-polarized waves. It is shown that the BRCS of a structure with a two-layer dielectric covering has oscillated character in a wide frequency range.

articleTitle: Microstrip antenna arrays with dielectric coating
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 7th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: In this work an algorithm for the calculation of the characteristics of microstrip antenna arrays (MSAA) with dielectric coating has been developed. Linear and square antenna arrays have been investigated. The following characteristics were obtained: antenna pattern, gain and VSWR. It was shown that changing of the dielectric coating parameters leads to substantial changes of the antenna array radiation characteristics.

articleTitle: The method of decomposition on eigenfunctions application to inhomogeneous coaxial cables simulation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 7th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: The method of decomposition on eigenfunctions has been extensively applied to the wave propagation simulation in inhomogeneous coaxial cable. It provides a comparatively faster algorithm for simulation and visualization of electromagnetic processes occurring in long coaxial lines. The method is applied to the simulation of cables with a steel partition, as well as the junction domain of layered cables. This method is extended and applied for the investigation of cables with different heterogeneity, as well as for different cable junction area simulation.

articleTitle: Finite photonic crystals implementation in microwave devices
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 7th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: A numerical model is given for a dielectric crystal with metallic rods inside it serving as defects. Useful software for the FPC (finite photonic crystal) simulation has been created. The results of simulation of some microwave devices are presented.

articleTitle: About self-organization and dispersion of eigen fields of a nonlinear dielectric layer
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 7th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: The open nonlinear electrodynamic system - nonlinear transverse nonhomogeneous dielectric layer - is an example of an inorganic system having the properties of self-organization which is peculiar to biological systems. The necessary precondition of the effects of self-organization is the presence of a flow of energy acting in the system from an external source, due to which the system gets the ability to form structures independently (see Loskutov, A.Yu. and Mikhailov, A.S., "Introduction into Synergetics", Nauka Publishers, 1990). On an example of the nonlinear transverse nonhomogeneous dielectric layer, the constructive approach of the analysis of amplitude/phase dispersion of eigen oscillation-wave fields of a nonlinear object, the norm of an eigen field is defined from the solution of a diffraction problem of plane waves or excitation of a point or compact source of a nonlinear layer.

articleTitle: Dynamic stress concentration in the vicinity of arbitrary-form hole in a half-space
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 7th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: The procedure to study the stresses in the vicinity of an arbitrary-form hole in an elastic half-space is proposed. The surface of the cavity is under time-variable pressure. The procedure is based on utilization of Fourier integral time transform and the null-field method.

articleTitle: The generalized functions method in the theory of symmetric dipole
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 7th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: In the problems of thin wire antennas, Hallen's integral equation is often used. Here we suggest an original method of transformation of Hallen's equation into Fredholm's integral equation of the second order having a symmetric singular kernel and a logarithmic feature.

articleTitle: Visualization of the latent body's shape and position based on the measured scattered field
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 7th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: In this article we present an algorithm for the shape and position (DSP) of a latent body determination based on the holographic principle with the help of the Method of Auxiliary Sources (MAS). The algorithm considered here allows one to resolve this problem with great accuracy even if the body being metallic or dielectric has a complicated shape. We also consider the problem connected with the embedded body. The corresponding numerical results are presented.

articleTitle: Near field distribution of thin impedance vibrators in absorbing medium
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 7th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: The asymptotic expression of the current in a thin impedance vibrator disposed in an homogeneous isotropic medium with sufficiently arbitrary parameters was obtained. Expressions of vibrator near fields as functions of electrical and physical characteristics of the medium were found. Calculations were carried out and their results represented as graphs of the dependence of near field distribution on medium parameters and surface impedance of the vibrators.

articleTitle: Modelling of nonlinear electromagnetic wave propagation in random discrete absorbing media
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 7th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: In this paper we suggest a method of computation of electromagnetic signal interaction with absorbing inhomogeneity in three-dimensional random discrete media. We model the process of wave multiple interaction with discrete inhomogeneity chaotically disposed in the layer media. The result of a computer imitation of the process on the basis of a stochastic model yields the distributions in space of co-ordinates of the energy of the scattering wave and energy of absorption wave dependent on interaction time.

articleTitle: The multi-band, multi-pitch antenna
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 7th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: A new design of multi-band, broadband multiple pitch helical antenna is presented. The proposed antenna is applicable for the use of portable transceivers to cover two bands of operating frequencies. The first band covers 150 MHz to 174 MHz. The second band covers 764 to 870 MHz. Dividing the helix into multiple segments with different pitches and number of turns to create multiple, overlapping resonances, a VSWR of better than 2:1 is achieved from 764 to 870 MHz. Also, by using a simple, two-element high-pass matching circuit, the antenna is matched to 50 ohms from 150 to 174 MHz without affecting the response in the second band. The radiation patterns of the antenna mounted on a portable radio chassis exhibit the characteristics of a dipole in both bands. The helical antenna remains as a single feeding, single element antenna.

articleTitle: Scattering and propagation in finite photonic crystals with complex material filling
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 7th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: The method of auxiliary sources (MAS) is used to study doped finite photonic crystals (FPC) with anisotropic, chiral or other complex material inclusions. The primitive cells of FPC are supposed to have a given crystallographic structure with certain defects, such as extrinsic inclusions, vacancies, dislocations and so on. An effective solution to the wave propagation and scattering problems in such crystals is obtained, an original treatment of eigenvalue and eigenfield problems in application to FPC is presented, and the FPC band structure is calculated, taking account of inter-cell interactions. A new computer code to analyze radiation, scattering, absorption and energetic characteristics of the doped FPC is described, and its possibilities for the design of integrated optic devices are demonstrated.

articleTitle: Software creation for the finite photonic crystals simulation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 7th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: Devices based on photonic crystals have recently gained great interest (see Joannopoulos, J., "Photonic Crystals: Modeling the flow of light", Princeton University Press, 1995). This is a fast developing area of science, with a promising future prospect. Such crystals might find use in variety of microwave devices - mixers, filters, etc. Development of such structures by experimental methods is either too expensive or impossible due to technical limitations. An engineer-oriented software package has been created for the development and simulation of PGB (photonic band gap) structures made of biisotropic and complex materials.

articleTitle: The embedded eigenvalues of the waveguide
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 7th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: Waveguide trapped modes, their existence and asymptotes are studied. Simple eigenvalues (embedded in the continuous spectrum) are shown not to be stable under a small perturbation of the waveguide filling, contrary to the behavior of isolated eigenvalues.

articleTitle: Diffraction effects in two-dimensional Gaussian focused wave beam in a moved acoustical medium
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 7th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: The plane problem of Gaussian wave beam focusing in the moving acoustic medium is considered. The influence of the velocity and the direction of the medium motion on diffraction effects in the focused beam is studied.

articleTitle: On the theory of symmetric short vibrator
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 7th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: The rigorous solution of Hallen's integral equation for a symmetric short vibrator is given. It is shown, that distribution of the linear axial current of the vibrator is presented as l(z')=M/spl radic/(1-(2z'/h)/sup 2/), where M is the known coefficient, z' - the axial coordinate of observation point on the surface of the vibrator, and h - its length.
